PBBM: COMMUTE TIME IN METRO MANILA SHOULD TAKE LESS THAN 1 HOUR

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said his administration is prioritizing improvements in public transportation to cut Metro Manila commuters' one-way travel time to under an hour.

"That's the goal," Marcos said in Episode 3 of the BBM Podcast, which aired Thursday. "Ang usually sa planning dapat ang commute… going to work at saka pag-uwi, 'yung one way should not, hindi dapat lumagpas sa isang oras."

The President said efficient public transit is key to addressing severe traffic congestion driven by overreliance on private vehicles, which he attributed to inadequate transport options.

"We've seen the examples around the world. 'Yung mga lugar na talagang sumobra na ang traffic dahil lahat ng tao walang public transport, walang bus, walang tren, walang subway," he said. "Siyempre lahat kailangan bumili ng sasakyan. Bibili ng motor, bibili ng auto. Kaya nagkaka-traffic nang husto. So, that's why we are continuing to make (the public transportation system) more efficient."

Among the initiatives cited by Marcos are the rehabilitation of the long-unused Dalian trains for MRT-3 and the construction of the Metro Manila Subway, which will connect Valenzuela City to Pasay City.

"These are solutions so that life will be a little easier, so that life will be more convenient, you know, going to work," Marcos said.
